job: Reworking the stdio transport's tool-launch path to confine the spawned command instead of running it in the host process.
outcome: Reference servers and SDKs ship stdio tool execution defaulting to an isolated process/container with allowlist and dropped privileges.
motivation: Patching a single command field is a symptom-fix; the launcher itself must be the enforcement point.

task.what: Move stdio tool launch behind a confined launcher
task.where: MCP reference server and SDK stdio adapter code
task.when: Between now and Q2 2027 release cycles
task.why: Enforcement must sit in the runtime, not the string
task.how: Separate process/container, command allowlist, dropped privileges

job: Changing the framework's default so tool commands launch inside an isolated boundary rather than directly in the agent process.
outcome: Popular flow builders default stdio tools to process isolation; raw in-host exec becomes an opt-in for trusted setups.
motivation: Launching tool commands in the agent process keeps drawing critical RCE advisories like the Flowise import flaw.

task.what: Default tool-server exec to isolated boundary
task.where: Flow-builder import path and tool-runner runtime
task.how: Per-server command allowlist, remote transport, sandbox

job: Replaying the one-click configuration-to-execution pattern across MCP hosts and publishing advisories that pin the root cause on the transport.
outcome: Continued critical advisories proving in-host stdio exec is unsafe, forcing maintainers to make isolation the shipped default.
motivation: The stdio adapter exists to run code, so demonstrating exploitability pressures the ecosystem to relocate enforcement.

task.where: MCP hosts, frameworks, public advisory channels
task.when: Ongoing through the runway to Q2 2027
task.how: Coordinated disclosure, CVE filings, PoC replay
